**Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport** ([IATA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IATA_airport_code "IATA airport code"): **OPO**, [ICAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICAO_airport_code "ICAO airport code"): **LPPR**) or simply **Porto Airport** (formerly *Pedras Rubras Airport*) is an [international airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_airport "International airport") near [Porto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porto "Porto") (Oporto), Portugal. It is located 11 km (6.8 mi) northwest of the [Clérigos Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clérigos_Church "Clérigos Church") (in the centre of Porto). Its location is split between the municipalities of [Maia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maia_Municipality "Maia Municipality"), [Matosinhos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matosinhos "Matosinhos") and [Vila do Conde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vila_do_Conde "Vila do Conde"). The airport is run by [ANA – Aeroportos de Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANA_–_Aeroportos_de_Portugal "ANA – Aeroportos de Portugal") and is currently the second-busiest in the country, based on aircraft operations; and the second-busiest in passengers, based on Aeroportos de Portugal traffic statistics, after [Lisbon Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Airport "Lisbon Airport") and before [Faro Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faro_Airport "Faro Airport"). The airport is a base for [easyJet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EasyJet "EasyJet"), [Ryanair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryanair "Ryanair"), [TAP Air Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TAP_Air_Portugal "TAP Air Portugal") and its subsidiary [TAP Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TAP_Express "TAP Express").

## Location

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Porto_Airport&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Location")]

The airport is surrounded by the municipalities of [Matosinhos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matosinhos_Municipality "Matosinhos Municipality") (to the south and west) and [Vila do Conde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vila_do_Conde_Municipality "Vila do Conde Municipality") (to the north) and [Maia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maia_Municipality "Maia Municipality") (to the east). It covers the parish of [Perafita, Lavra e Santa Cruz do Bispo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perafita,_Lavra_e_Santa_Cruz_do_Bispo "Perafita, Lavra e Santa Cruz do Bispo") (in Matosinhos); Aveleda and Vilar do Pinheiro (Vila do Conde); and Vila Nova da Telha and [Moreira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moreira_(Maia) "Moreira (Maia)") (Maia).[[2]](#cite_note-PDA1-2) It includes an area of between 72 metres (236 ft) in the extreme south and 43 metres (141 ft) in the north.[[2]](#cite_note-PDA1-2)[*[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")*] The southern portion of the airport intersects the hydrographic watershed of the Leça River, while the north is crossed by effluents of Onda River.[[2]](#cite_note-PDA1-2)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Porto_Airport&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

The airport around Porto opened in 1945 and was initially known as *Pedras Rubras Airport*, after the name for the locality where the airport is located: [Pedras Rubras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedras_Rubras "Pedras Rubras") ("red rocks"). It is still known by this name in the region. The land on which the airport was built was originally agricultural, characterised by rich soils that permitted the cultivation of various cereals.[[2]](#cite_note-PDA1-2)

It was renamed in 1990 after former Portuguese prime minister, [Francisco de Sá Carneiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_de_Sá_Carneiro "Francisco de Sá Carneiro"), who died in a plane crash when he was traveling to this airport on 4 December 1980.[[3]](#cite_note-porto-airport-car-rental.com-3)

Along with the airports in [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon"), [Faro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faro,_Portugal "Faro, Portugal"), [Ponta Delgada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponta_Delgada "Ponta Delgada"), [Santa Maria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Maria_(Tavira) "Santa Maria (Tavira)"), [Horta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horta,_Azores "Horta, Azores"), [Flores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flores_Island,_Azores "Flores Island, Azores"), [Madeira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madeira_Island "Madeira Island"), and [Porto Santo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porto_Santo_Island "Porto Santo Island"), the airport's concessions to provide support to civil aviation were conceded to [ANA Aeroportos de Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANA_Aeroportos_de_Portugal "ANA Aeroportos de Portugal") on 18 December 1998, under provisions of decree 404/98. With this concession, ANA became responsible for the planning, development and construction of future infrastructure.[[3]](#cite_note-porto-airport-car-rental.com-3)

A new terminal building, designed by Portuguese firm ICQ, was built between 2003 and 2006, and became operational in the last quarter of 2006.[[4]](#cite_note-www.airport-technology.com/projects/oporto/-4)

Porto Airport reached ten million passengers in a year for the first time on 6 December 2017.[[5]](#cite_note-5)[*[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")*]
